manifest.title: Private Nostr Relay
manifest.author: Marcus Quinn <marcus@marcusquinn.com>
manifest.description:
A private [Nostr](https://nostr.com) relay powered by
[strfry](https://github.com/hoytech/strfry).

Only the public keys you list can publish events. Every other write is
rejected, so the relay never becomes an open public relay. Anyone who knows
the address can still read events, so treat published content as public unless
it is encrypted.

### Features

* Fast strfry relay with an LMDB database stored in Cloudron backups
* Write allowlist of `npub` or hexadecimal public keys, read on every event, so
  changes apply without a restart
* Starts closed: an empty allowlist rejects every write
* NIP-11 relay information (name, description, contact, operator key) set
  through app environment variables
* Real client IP addresses from Cloudron's reverse proxy
manifest.tagline: Private Nostr relay with allowlisted writes
manifest.postInstallMessage: The relay rejects every write until you add an npub or hexadecimal public key to /app/data/allowlist.txt. See the Allowlist guide before connecting a client.
manifest.changelog:
* Initial Cloudron package for a private strfry 1.1.3 Nostr relay.
* Writes are limited to public keys in `/app/data/allowlist.txt`, as `npub` (checksum-verified) or hexadecimal. An empty allowlist rejects every write.
* NIP-11 relay name, description, contact and operator key are set with app environment variables.
* The database size is not capped, and the relay starts within Cloudron's open-file limit.

manifest.tagline: Private Nostr relay with allowlisted writes
manifest.postInstallMessage:
Your relay URL is `wss://$CLOUDRON-APP-FQDN`.

The relay **rejects every write** until you add a public key to
`/app/data/allowlist.txt`, one `npub` or hexadecimal key per line. Edit the
file with this app's **File Manager** or **Web Terminal**. Changes apply to the
next event without a restart.

Reads are public. Never put a private key (`nsec`) in the allowlist. See the
[allowlist guide](https://github.com/marcusquinn/cloudron-nostr-relay-app/blob/main/docs/ALLOWLIST.md).

allowlist-writer.message: Add at least one npub or hexadecimal public key to `/app/data/allowlist.txt` with the File Manager. Until then the relay rejects every write.

manifest.changelog:
* The post-install message shows the `wss://` relay URL and how to edit the allowlist from the File Manager or Web Terminal.
* A dashboard checklist item reminds you to add the first allowlist key.
